title: The light placed in you
hookLine: the body came into the world when the Lord placed His light within it (Anand, the body pauris)

lines: A SCREEN, A FLICKER, TWO PARENTS.
cards: A dim room, a gray screen, two parents holding hands. The technician moves the wand and points: there. A tiny flicker, fast as a bird's wing.
Many parents say that moment changed something; before it there was news, and after it there was someone. Nobody in the room could say exactly what had arrived.
The Anand has an answer, and it's the next thing Guru Amar Das says to the body.

teach.h: O MY BODY, AGAIN: NOT A QUESTION NOW.
teach.b: The pauri starts as yesterday's did, ae sareeraa mairiaa. But this time it doesn't ask; it tells.

teach.h: JOT: THE LORD'S LIGHT, PLACED IN YOU.
teach.b: In paraphrase: the Lord placed His light within you, and then you came into the world. And it says it twice, turning the line around, as if to make sure it's heard.
The word is jot, light, the same word Sikhs use for the one light that passed from Guru Nanak to each Guru after him. Here that light is placed in every body.

teach.h: FIRST THE LIGHT, THEN THE ARRIVAL.
teach.b: Notice the order: first the light, then the arrival. The body doesn't earn the light later by being good; it comes into the world because the light is already in it.

teach.h: MOTHER AND FATHER, AND THE WORLD A PLAY.
teach.b: The pauri goes on: the Lord is Himself mother and Himself father, the One who made living beings and showed them the world.
By the Guru's grace someone understands, and then the whole world is seen as a play, chalat, the Lord's own wonderful display.

It closes with the signature line: the One who made the root of creation placed His light in you, and then you came into the world. Yesterday's question was hard: what have you done? Today's line is the ground under it.
Whatever the body has or hasn't done, the light was placed there first. Many Sikhs hear this as the reason no one can be looked down on: every body in the room arrived the same way.

how: Many Sikhs recite the full Anand Sahib each morning, and the teaching that the one divine light, jot, dwells in every body is often given as a reason Sikhs reject caste and serve all in langar alike.

o: a spark earned by doing good deeds
a flame lit in the gurdwara at dusk
light, placed by the Lord in every body

games.q: the light pauri — tap the pairs.
p: first the light, then the arrival

s: in this pauri the body earns the light later by being good
the light is placed first; then the body comes into the world.
the pauri says the same line twice, turned around
the Lord placed His light in you, and then you came into the world.
jot is also the word Sikhs use for the light passed from Guru to Guru
the one light that passed from Guru Nanak to each Guru after him.

games.q: the Anand tells the body how it came into the world. what does it say came first?
o: the body, and the light was added at a ceremony.
the light, and then the body came into the world.
good deeds, and the light was the reward.
games.why: the pauri says the Lord placed His light in the body, and then it came into the world: the light is there before anything is done.

practice: Lay two fingers lightly on the inside of your wrist, below the thumb, or at the side of your neck, and wait until you find your pulse.

Don't count; just feel it arrive, again and again, without being asked: you didn't start it, and you aren't running it. If the Anand's line helps, let it ride along with the beat, and if you pray, say Waheguru once, softly.

wordCard.voice: Jot, light. In the Anand, the Lord places His jot in the body, and only then does the body come into the world.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: jot, light; the Lord's light placed in the body, and the light Sikhs say passed through the ten Gurus.

carryVoice: Your line: light in the body. It was placed there before you ever arrived. Three hundred ninety-five days, and counting.

sources.ref: Ramkali M3, Anand, the light pauri (ae sareeraa mairiaa har tum meh jot rakhee), Ang 921
